metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent demonstrated GIMP menu navigation. Image rotation (Image > Transform > Rotate 90° clockwise) is a one-click operation accessible through the Image menu.
metadata.capability_extraction: Agent can use GIMP menu operations. Rotation via Image > Transform is a single menu selection with no dialog configuration required.
metadata.failure_analysis: Original task required layer drag-and-drop which the agent executed incorrectly. Rotation is a simpler whole-image transformation that requires only menu navigation.
metadata.task_rationale: Rotating the image is the simplest whole-image transformation in GIMP — one menu selection, no drag. The result is easily verified by checking whether the exported PNG changed from landscape (2192x1118) to portrait (1118x2192) orientation.
metadata.explanation: The getter downloads the exported PNG and checks if height > width (portrait orientation). Original image is landscape (2192x1118); after 90° rotation it becomes portrait (1118x2192). Metric returns 1.0 if portrait. Initial state has no PNG, so initial score is 0.0.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly downloads and checks the exported PNG at the right path (/home/user/Desktop/orange_background.png), verifying both the filename and export location requirements.
Metric correctly uses portrait orientation (height > width) as a proxy for 90° rotation: the original image is landscape (2192x1118), so after any 90° rotation it becomes portrait (1118x2192).
Initial state resistance is good: no PNG file exists initially, so getter returns error dict and metric returns 0.0.
No postconfig needed since verification is file-based rather than UI-state-dependent.
Metric correctly handles the rule-type expected parameter by ignoring it (rules dict is {}), which is appropriate since no expected values are needed.
Minor limitation: evaluator checks portrait orientation but cannot distinguish 90° clockwise from 90° counter-clockwise — both produce the same portrait dimensions from a landscape source.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional: To distinguish CW from CCW rotation, the getter could use PIL's EXIF or compare pixel samples (e.g., top-left corner color). However, for practical purposes the orientation proxy is sufficient since the task's primary verification goal is confirming a 90° rotation was performed.
